title.narrative: Emergency response to provide access to comprehensive WASH services in North Gaza

description.narrative: ltpgtACF aims to provide life-saving support to ltbgt5500 lt/bgtIDPsltbgt across the Gaza Strip, with a focus on locations in Deir al Balah, Gaza City, and Khan Yunis,lt/bgt through this Emergency WASH project, ensuring access to safe water, sanitation, solid waste management, and hygiene promotion in shelters and displacement sites. ACF will provide a holistic package of services in the targeted location, aiming to improve the overall WASH conditions for all IDPs residing in the area.ltbrgtThis intervention will expand ACF’s water supply programming by supporting returnees by trucking ltbgt3,180 m3lt/bgt of drinking water, ensuring a minimum of 6 liters per capita per day for drinking and cooking in line with WASH Cluster guidelines. ACF will support returning IDPs by supplying ltbgt3,180lt/bgt ltbgtm3lt/bgt of drinking water and facilitate fuel supply through the UNOPS arrangement to operate wells while aiding public water services in repairing damaged infrastructure. Water quality and delivery will be monitored in coordination with WASH partners, adhering to the standards of the Water Accessibility Technical Working Group. ltbrgtTo address urgent sanitation needs, ACF will construct 50 new latrines and rehabilitate existing facilities in shelters and camps. This intervention will prioritize vulnerable households, including female-headed families, persons with disabilities, and the elderly. Where possible, latrines will be connected to sanitation networks otherwise, cesspit tanks and desludging services will be implemented. Existing latrines in collective shelters will be rehabilitated in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and UNRWA. Community involvement will be encouraged to ensure sustainability, and monitoring mechanisms will track progress to maintain functionality and effectiveness. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtSolid waste management will be enhanced to address the growing health risks from waste accumulation in displacement sites. This intervention will expand collection and transfer operations in coordination with municipalities and solid waste councils. ACF will activate agreements with local service providers and ensure the provision of fuel through UNOPS to maintain consistent waste removal. Waste collection workers will receive PPE to ensure their safety. Monitoring mechanisms will track service delivery, while coordination with the WASH Cluster and Solid Waste Task Force will help address gaps and optimize resources. ltbrgtHygiene promotion activities will be implemented to reduce disease risks in overcrowded shelters. ACF will work with community committees and trained representatives to conduct awareness campaigns on best hygiene practices, as identified through WASH Cluster recommendations and MEAL activities. Key messaging will be tailored to ensure appropriate responses. This will include initiatives such as water container cleaning campaigns. To support improved hygiene practices, ACF will provide IDPs in shelters with essential cleaning materials and tools for maintaining latrines, cleaning water storage, and ensuring safe water handling. These materials will be sourced locally and distributed in coordination with the Ministry of Social Development to reach the most vulnerable shelters. ACF will closely monitor the implementation of hygiene promotion activities and collaborate with the Hygiene Working Group to ensure best practices are followed. ltbrgtThroughout this Emergency WASH project, ACF will coordinate with the WASH Cluster, local authorities, and technical working groups to optimize resource allocation, avoid duplication, and ensure adherence to humanitarian standards. By integrating water access, sanitation, waste management, and hygiene promotion, ACF aims to provide comprehensive, life-saving support while strengthening community resilience in affected areas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
